title: Range of the Absolute Value Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Determine the range of f(x)=|x| over all real inputs.

steps.title: Use Nonnegativity of |x|
steps.explanation: Distance from zero is never negative by definition of absolute value.
steps.why: The absolute value outputs max(x, -x), which is always >= 0.

steps.title: Check Zero Is Attained
steps.explanation: The input x=0 produces the smallest possible output 0, so the endpoint is included.
steps.why: Range membership requires an actual preimage, and 0 has one.

steps.title: Check All Positives Occur
steps.explanation: Any positive target a is reached at x=a, and arbitrarily large outputs arise from large inputs.
steps.why: Every nonnegative value is its own absolute value, so nothing above 0 is missed.

steps.title: Conclude
steps.explanation: The outputs are precisely the nonnegative reals.
steps.why: Combining the lower bound with attainment of every value above it gives the closed ray.
